title: Practitioner Visit Documentation for Continued CGM Coverage, Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program
content:
Clinical documentation requirement of the Continuous Glucose Monitoring Supply Program: practitioner visits that qualify the first authorization and keep refills covered.

## Requirements

1. **Initial qualification.** On tiers where the initial visit look-back is greater than 0, the first authorization grant of a CGM program is recorded only when a medical record with purpose initial qualification documents an in-person or telehealth visit with the treating practitioner dated no more than the tier's initial visit look-back, in calendar months, before the order date of the written order it rests on.
2. **Follow-up.** On tiers where the follow-up visit interval is greater than 0, a refill ships only when the most recent visit date on the program's medical records with purpose continued-need follow-up or initial qualification is no more than the tier's follow-up visit interval, in calendar months, before the ship date, counted in calendar months back from the ship date with the same calendar day allowed (the last day of the month when that day does not exist). The visit documents that the customer is using the CGM and following the diabetes treatment plan.
3. **No cure by statement.** A missing or out-of-date follow-up visit is not cured by the customer's statement that a visit took place: Larkfield requests the visit note from the practitioner and records it when received, and until then the refill does not ship, and the program may be held for documentation lapse under the program's hold and closure rules only when its authorization has also lapsed.
4. **Self-pay.** On the CGM Self-Pay Program no visit requirement applies.

## Follow-up boundary (hypothetical figures)

Suppose a follow-up interval of 6 months and a ship date of 20 September:

| Most recent qualifying visit date | Refill may ship |
|---|---|
| 20 March of the same year (exactly 6 calendar months back, same calendar day) | Yes |
| 19 March of the same year | No |
| 2 June of the same year | Yes |

Counting back from a ship date of 31 August with a 6-month interval reaches February, which has no 31st day; the boundary falls on the last day of February, and a visit on that day is in time.

## Records that count

Only medical records with purpose continued-need follow-up or initial qualification count toward the follow-up requirement; a clinical document recorded for another purpose serves only that purpose.
